utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Eastvale' by name among the cities in its service area.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Eastvale was a named member city of Western Community Energy (WCE), but WCE deregistered with the CPUC and dissolved via Chapter 9 bankruptcy in 2021 and no longer operates. No CCA currently serves Eastvale or anywhere in Riverside County. SCE is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Eastvale Community Development Department, Building Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: eastvaleca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session. This department name and page content is confirmed only via search-engine indexing of the city's own page, not independently read.

permit_url.notes: URL identified via search-engine indexing; eastvaleca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so its content could not be independently read or verified.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Eastvale/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

required_documents.notes: eastvaleca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, blocking access to any solar-specific submittal requirements beyond a general search-engine summary indicating a 'Combination Building Permit' application and racking/attachment documentation are required.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Search-engine synthesis indicates the Building Safety Division has piloted SolarApp+ for detached single-family residential PV installations, but this could not be independently confirmed via direct fetch this session.
